# zuregex

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

zuregex is a regular expression package that matches with a bundled
[PCRE2](https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2), the same version on every
platform, from R and from C.

Base R's `perl = TRUE` uses PCRE2 too. zuregex adds what that leaves out:

* Capture groups come back as a data frame, one column per group.
* A pattern is compiled once and cached, and matching runs on several
  threads where the build has OpenMP.
* Replacements use PCRE2's full template language: groups by name, past
  nine, with defaults and case forcing.
* Other packages reach the same PCRE2 from C through `LinkingTo`, instead
  of bundling a copy.

## Installation

Install zuregex from CRAN with:

``` r
install.packages("zuregex")
```

Or install the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuregex")
```

## Usage

```{r}
library(zuregex)
```

`re_match()` turns the named groups of a pattern into the columns of a data
frame, one row per string. The last string is not a log line, so its row
is `NA`.

```{r}
log <- c(
  "2026-10-21 08:15:02 GET /index.html 200 512",
  "2026-10-21 08:15:09 POST /login 302 0",
  "2026-10-21 08:16:44 GET /missing 404 128",
  "not a log line"
)
pattern <- "(?<time>\\S+ \\S+) (?<method>[A-Z]+) (?<path>\\S+) (?<status>\\d+)"
re_match(log, pattern)
```

zuregex also detects, extracts, replaces and splits with the same patterns;
[Get started](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/articles/zuregex.html)
walks through them on this log.

## Learn more

* [Get started](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/articles/zuregex.html)
  takes the log above through every main function.
* [Move from base R and stringr](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/articles/from-base-r.html)
  maps `grepl()`, `sub()`, `regmatches()` and the `str_*()` functions onto
  `re_*()`, and shows what behaves differently.
* [Bound the work of a match](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/articles/limits.html)
  sets match, depth and heap limits for patterns or input you do not
  trust.
* [Link to zuregex from C](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/articles/c-api.html)
  uses the bundled PCRE2 from another package's C code.
* The [reference index](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/reference/)
  lists every function, grouped as the API is.

zuregex builds on PCRE2, which backtracks. For matching in linear time, use
[re2](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=re2).
